newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi government dismisses customs strike threat.
newsitem.headline: Malawi government dismisses customs strike threat.

text.p: Malawian finance minister Aleke Banda on Monday stood firm against threats by more than 400 customs workers to go on strike in support of wage demands.
Malawi's Customs Workers Union threatened at the weekend to join a month-old civil servant strike from Tuesday. Eighty percent of government revenue comes from customs.
Banda said the government had no money to meet the demands and would not allow customs workers to close border posts because it would hurt the country's economy.
"We'll find means to keep the customs posts working," he told Reuters.

He said some employees were willing to go to work and would be protected by the government. "The security forces have a duty to protect those who want to work. We have no doubt we'll keep the posts working," he added.
The nationwide strike was called by the Civil Servants' Trade Union to push for a 100 percent wage increase.
However the government has said it can only afford a maximum 47 percent pay increase for its 100,000-strong workforce without upsetting the economy.
"Economic programmes are working well. If we did anything that rekindled inflation, everyone will be the loser," Banda said.

Malawi has introduced a reform programme aimed at increasing government efficiency and cutting public spending. Official figures show the economy grew by more than nine percent in 1996 and growth of 7.1 percent is projected for 1997.
